key_insight: QAOA is a useful benchmark for revealing how distributed quantum-network topology, entanglement handling, and switch scheduling jointly affect performance.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides design guidance for quantum data-center architects on how topology and resource provisioning change communication latency and entanglement overhead in distributed quantum computing.
method: Adapted QAOA to SwitchQNet with a routing generator that turns graph cost terms into remote-CX communication requests.
Evaluated distributed execution on Clos, fat-tree, and spine-leaf topologies.
Measured latency, EPR-pair overhead, EPR wait time, retry overhead, and sensitivity to network and hardware parameters.
evidence_signal: Across the tested topologies and parameter sweeps, QAOA showed modest but consistent latency reductions, with performance varying by buffer size, look-ahead depth, communication-qubit count, EPR latency, and EPR fidelity assumptions.
watch_item: The reported gains are modest and depend on simulator/architecture assumptions, so real hardware behavior may differ substantially.
paper_title: Performance Analysis of QAOA Across Distributed Quantum Network Topologies Using SwitchQNet
